verdicts.evidence: Numerical audit of the supporting-score identity f(h)+(p-h)f'(h)<=f(p) on 99×100 grids for L1, L2, and KL yields zero oracle identity error, zero constant-target score, and supporting-plane violations at machine-precision (1.11e-16), confirming no classifier can beat the constant 1-alpha predictor under perfect conditional coverage.

The logbook only re-aggregates the authors' official results.csv (not a fresh classifier run) and obtains 68.929% and 33.671%, which do not match the paper's claimed 68.4% and 38.3%; no independent experiment was executed to determine which values are correct.

Independent synthetic experiment on the paper's 8D heteroscedastic model (X~U([-1,1]^8), Y~N(0,sigma(X_1))) with analytic L1 miscoverage 0.0948 shows L1-ERT recovering 92% of the analytic violation at 30k test points (0.0866) while unaligned CovGap recovers only 5% (0.0049), with oracle-group CovGap staying near theory (0.0953).

The same 30,000-point synthetic run estimates over-coverage at 0.0445 (analytic 0.0460) and under-coverage at 0.0464 (analytic 0.0488), both nonzero and close to theory, confirming the asymmetric decomposition separates over- and under-coverage.

The logbook only reads the authors' released classification CSV (80 rows) and checks internal consistency (additive identity residual 8.94e-8) and directional gaps; no classification experiment was re-run, so the divergent KL values are not independently verified.

Mutation control with 20 seeds, 2,000 observations, and 5 folds shows in-sample evaluation of a label memorizer produces false ERT of 0.08886 while cross-fitted evaluation yields 0, and a genuine two-region signal is still detected at 0.01013, confirming k-fold cross-fitting prevents overfitting without erasing real signal.

overall: The logbook independently verifies claims 1, 3, 4, and 6 through executed code with concrete numerical results on non-toy setups. Claims 2 and 5 are inconclusive because they consist solely of re-aggregating or reading the authors' released output artifacts without fresh experiments, and Claim 2's numbers do not match the paper's reported values.
